description: Grow a network that refuses root, trunk, and leaves. Recursive branching creates a scaffold, then lateral reconnections turn that scaffold into a mesh where any point can connect to any other. Adjusting reconnection probability moves the artifact between tree and rhizome, making hierarchy versus multiplicity a concrete topological choice. It brings Deleuze and Guattari into graph theory by questioning when a tree is the wrong model.

description: A punching bag hanging from a fixed anchor via a cone-twist joint. The cone-twist constraint limits the bag's swing to a 45-degree cone while allowing only 15 degrees of twist — like a ball-and-socket joint with angular limits. The joint's bias and softness parameters control how sharply the limits are enforced.

description: A motorized drawbridge attached to a stone tower via a hinge joint. The motor rotates the bridge up and down within an 85-degree arc. description: A dual-hinge gimbal system with independent yaw and pitch control. Two motor-driven hinges are stacked orthogonally: one rotates freely around the vertical axis (yaw), the other is limited to plus-or-minus 45 degrees on the horizontal axis (pitch). Together they aim a payload in 3D space. The idle mode sweeps smoothly through a Lissajous-like pattern; arrow keys override with direct motor control. This demonstrates how composing multiple single-axis joints creates multi-axis articulation.

description: A motorized crank mechanism combining three joint types into one machine. A hinge joint spins a wheel at constant velocity, a pin joint connects the wheel to a sliding rod, and a slider joint guides the rod along a rail. The result is rotary-to-linear conversion — the fundamental mechanism behind pistons, steam engines, and sewing machines. Watch how continuous rotation becomes reciprocating translation through the geometry of constraint.
